# A quantitative inball for a base-balanced moment body

Use the notation of `candidate b4c3b9c6a52059d2`:
mu is mixed volume on a compact convex body, j is a positive-volume
integer fiber K=C_j, its volume is w>0, and T=T_max(j) is the attained
maximum mass of a dominated source with integer centroid j. Its mass-t
moment body M_t(j) is defined for 0<t<=T.

For every 0<t<T, the body M_t(j) has nonempty continuous interior.
More quantitatively, let K contain an ordinary Euclidean ball of radius
r>0. Choose any 0<s<min(t,w). Then M_t(j) contains a translate of

    [(T-t)s/(t(T-s))] [1-(s/w)^(1/d)] K.                (1)

In particular its inradius is at least

    [(T-t)s/(t(T-s))] [1-(s/w)^(1/d)] r>0.             (2)

Every point of this contained body is represented by a dominated
submeasure of the original mixed measure with mass t and integer
centroid j. No new fiber points or new source mass are inserted.

## Proof

Let Z_s(K) denote the set of centroids of all submeasures of ordinary
volume on K having mass s. Put theta=(s/w)^(1/d), so 0<theta<1.
For every p in K, the homothetic body

    K_p=(1-theta)p+theta K

lies in K by convexity, has volume s, and has centroid
(1-theta)p+theta g_K. Therefore

    (1-theta)K+theta g_K subset Z_s(K).                (3)

Choose an attained mass-T base-balanced submeasure sigma_T<=mu and
write its continuous centroid as g_T. Set

    lambda=(t-s)/(T-s),  nu=(T-t)/(T-s).

These numbers are positive, sum to one, and satisfy lambda T+nu s=t.
For any mass-s submeasure sigma_s on the single fiber {j}xK, the
measure lambda sigma_T+nu sigma_s is dominated by mu, has mass t,
and has integer first moment tj. Its continuous centroid is

    (lambda T/t)g_T+(nu s/t)g_(sigma_s).

Consequently M_t(j) contains a translate of (nu s/t)Z_s(K). Applying
(3) gives (1), and an inball of K gives (2). This proves all assertions.

## A cap-cover consequence with no extra nondegeneracy assumption

Suppose finitely many caps

    H_i={u_i.x+a_i.(z-j)-b_i>=0},  |u_i|=1,

cover the entire fiber {j}xK, and let

    Psi_i=integral [u_i.x+a_i.(z-j)-b_i]_+ dmu.

The attained cover certificate in
`candidate a5428a02cd85fb48` supplies nonnegative
weights lambda_i summing to one with

    sum_i lambda_i Psi_i >= t inradius(M_t(j)).

Combining with (2) proves the explicit strict lower bound

    sum_i lambda_i Psi_i
       >= [(T-t)s/(T-s)] [1-(s/w)^(1/d)] r>0.          (4)

One may, for example, take t=D_j/2 and
s=min(D_j/4,w/2). The proved inequality T>=D_j>=w>0 ensures all
strict inequalities needed above. Thus the moment-body inball used in
the cover-hinge bridge is always available below the marginal capacity;
it need not be assumed separately. The result concerns hinge integrals,
not an OC cap-volume lower bound.
